topic: registry-core: core cast (persons), organisations and locations with role history

properties.profile: President of Nepal since 13 March 2023, succeeding Bidya Devi Bhandari. Member of the Nepali Congress until 2023, then left active party membership after the presidential election (Wikipedia). Earlier Speaker of the House of Representatives (1994-1999), Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister (2000-2001). In September 2025 he administered the oath to the Karki interim ministers at Shital Niwas.

Chairman of CPN-UML (2014-2018; again from 2021). Prime Minister three times: 12 Oct 2015-4 Aug 2016, 15 Feb 2018-13 Jul 2021 and 15 Jul 2024 to September 2025. He resigned on 9 September 2025 during the Gen Z protests; Wikipedia's biography gives 12 September 2025 as the end of the term, the date Sushila Karki took over. After the 5 March 2026 election (he lost Jhapa-5 to Balen Shah, per Wikipedia) he was detained on 28 March 2026 following the recommendation of the government commission on the protest deaths; the Supreme Court declined to release him and Ramesh Lekhak (reported 31 March 2026). The NHRC report held him primarily responsible for the rights violations (reported 27 May 2026).

evidence.note: End of third term: resignation 9 Sept 2025 (Fourth Oli Cabinet page) versus 12 Sept 2025 (K. P. Sharma Oli page, date of successor).

properties.profile: Known as Prachanda. Prime Minister 2008-2009, 2016-2017 and 26 Dec 2022-15 Jul 2024. Chair of the CPN (Maoist Centre) until it merged into the Nepali Communist Party on 4-5 November 2025; coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025. Leader of the opposition 15 Jul 2024-12 Sep 2025. Member of the House for Eastern Rukum 1 since 26 March 2026 (Wikipedia).

President of the Nepali Congress from 7 March 2016 to 16 January 2026, when Gagan Thapa was recognised as president. Prime Minister five times, most recently 13 Jul 2021-26 Dec 2022. Leader of the opposition 2022-2024. Wikipedia reports that his residence was attacked and set on fire on 9 September 2025 and that he and his wife, Arzu Rana Deuba, were injured.

Former Chief Justice of Nepal (acting from 11 July 2016, retired June 2017). Sworn in as interim Prime Minister on 12 September 2025 and held the office until 27 March 2026; the first woman to be Prime Minister. Wikipedia reports that Gen Z organisers selected her name in an online Discord poll. The House of Representatives was dissolved on 12 September 2025 and elections were set for 5 March 2026. On 8 March 2026 she received the report of the commission headed by Gauri Bahadur Karki.

Prime Minister 6 Feb-29 Aug 2011; chairman of CPN (UML) 2009-2014. In the CPN (Unified Socialist) 2021-2025; senior leader of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025. The Wikipedia article on the 2025 protests lists his residence among the buildings set on fire.

Chairperson of the Rastriya Swatantra Party (founded 1 July 2022). Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister 26 Dec 2022-27 Jan 2023 and 6 Mar-15 Jul 2024. Arrested 4 April 2025 in a cooperative fraud case; freed from Nakkhu prison on 9 September 2025 during the protests, returned on 13 September, and released on bail on 19 December 2025 (Wikipedia; release reported by Himal Press). Returned to the RSP headquarters on 21 December 2025 after 261 days.

Nepali Congress general secretary 16 Dec 2021-14 Jan 2026; Health Minister 2016-2017. Elected unopposed as party president at the second special general convention (11-14 January 2026); the Election Commission recognised the new leadership on 16 January 2026. Lost the Sarlahi 4 seat in the March 2026 election (Wikipedia).

Chairman of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party since 5 December 2021. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation 17 Jan-25 Feb 2023. Member of the House for Jhapa 3 from 2018 until the dissolution on 12 September 2025.
Prime Minister 25 May 2009-6 Feb 2011. Chairman of the CPN (Unified Socialist) from 18 Aug 2021 until its merger on 4 Nov 2025; co-coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025.

Chairman of the Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal (the party's English name on Wikipedia is People's Socialist Party, Nepal) since its founding on 22 April 2020. Deputy Prime Minister 1 Jun 2018-24 Dec 2019 and 10 Mar-13 May 2024; Foreign Minister 2008-2009 and 2011. Member of the House from 2 May 2023 until its dissolution on 12 September 2025.

evidence.note: The Upendra Yadav page's infobox gives his party chairmanship as 2020-2023; the party's own page gives 2020-present.

properties.profile: Prime Minister 29 Aug 2011-14 Mar 2013; Finance Minister 2008-2009. Founded the Naya Shakti Party in 2016. Chairman of the Pragatisheel Loktantrik Party from 20 November 2025 (Wikipedia).

Nepali Congress politician. Home Minister from 15 July 2024; resigned on 8 September 2025, the day of the police firing, taking 'moral responsibility'. Detained on 28 March 2026 after the government commission recommended a criminal investigation; the Supreme Court declined to release him and Oli (reported 31 March 2026).

evidence.note: Death toll at the time of his resignation: Himal Press says 19, Wikipedia's Lekhak page says 23.

properties.profile: CPN (UML). Minister of Communication and Information Technology from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025; Chief Minister of Gandaki Province 2018-2021. In April 2025 he said platforms that defied the government's call to register would be banned. The NHRC termed the 2023 directive behind the restriction unconstitutional and recommended action against him (reported 27 May 2026).

CPN (UML). Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister from 15 July 2024. Forced out on 9 September 2025 with Oli (his own Wikipedia page); the Fourth Oli Cabinet page gives 12 September 2025 for the end of his term.

evidence.note: End of term: 9 Sept 2025 (person page) versus 12 Sept 2025 (cabinet page).

properties.profile: Nepali Congress. Foreign Minister from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Wikipedia reports that she and Sher Bahadur Deuba were injured and taken into police custody after their house was attacked and set on fire on 9 September 2025.

Chief of the Army Staff since 9 September 2024; appointed on the Council of Ministers' recommendation and announced on 28 August 2024, succeeding Prabhu Ram Sharma. Wikipedia credits him with facilitating the dialogue between Gen Z protest leaders and the political leadership in September 2025.

Known as Balen. Elected Mayor of Kathmandu as an independent in May 2022; resigned on 18 January 2026 to contest the 5 March 2026 election. Joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party (from 28 December 2025 per Wikipedia), won Jhapa 5 defeating KP Sharma Oli, and was sworn in as Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. The Ministry of Defence and the Prime Minister's Office websites list him as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

Managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority 2016-2020 and 2021 until his removal on 24 March 2025. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as minister of energy, water resources and irrigation, also holding urban development and physical infrastructure in the Karki interim government; resigned 7 January 2026. Chairman of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party from 10 January 2026. Wikipedia lists him among the candidates discussed for interim prime minister.

Founder of Hami Nepal, the youth NGO that called the 8 September 2025 protest and, per Wikipedia, liaised between organisers and the Nepali Army afterwards. Joined the RSP on 18 January 2026, won Gorkha 1 on 9 March 2026, became Home Minister on 27 March 2026, resigned on 22 April 2026 citing moral responsibility amid a controversy over his financial conduct, and was reappointed on 9 June 2026 after an inquiry cleared him (ShareSansar, Wikipedia). The Ministry of Home Affairs website names him as minister (accessed 2026-10-05; Nepali spelling there: Sudhan Gurung).

evidence.note: Spelling: Sudan Gurung (English reporting) versus Sudhan Gurung (Ministry of Home Affairs site).

properties.profile: Advocate. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as Minister of Home Affairs in the Karki interim government, also holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs until 22 September 2025. Home Minister until 26 March 2026; succeeded by Sudan Gurung.

Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as finance minister in the Karki interim government at Shital Niwas. The Kathmandu Post spells his name 'Rameshore Khanal'; the Karki cabinet page on Wikipedia lists 'Rameshwar Khanal' as finance minister until 27 March 2026.

evidence.note: Name spelling differs across sources: Rameshore / Rameshwar / Rameshwor.

properties.profile: Chief District Officer of Kathmandu during the protests of 8-9 September 2025. Arrested from his home in Koteshwor on 31 March 2026 by the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office after the government commission's recommendation (Himalayan Times). The commission recommended action against him under Section 182 (Onlinekhabar). Deccan Herald's report of the 9 September curfew notice gives his name as 'Chhabilal Rijal'.

evidence.note: Name spelling: Chhabi Rijal (Himalayan Times, Onlinekhabar) versus Chhabilal Rijal (Deccan Herald via search snippet).

properties.profile: CPN (UML). Speaker of the House of Representatives from 19 January 2023; Wikipedia gives 19 January 2026 as the end of his term. Member for Jhapa 2 until the dissolution on 12 September 2025. Succeeded as Speaker by Dol Prasad Aryal on 5 April 2026.

evidence.note: Wikipedia gives the end of his speakership as 19 Jan 2026, while the House was dissolved on 12 Sept 2025 and his successor took office on 5 Apr 2026; the interval is not explained in the sources retrieved.

properties.profile: Chief Justice of Nepal from 6 October 2024 until his retirement on 31 March 2026, appointed by President Ram Chandra Paudel. Not the same person as Deputy Prime Minister Prakash Man Singh. Followed by Sapana Pradhan Malla as acting Chief Justice.

Inspector General of Nepal Police. The cabinet appointed him on 29 August 2025 to replace Deepak Thapa; he assumed office as the 32nd IGP on 4 September 2025, days before the protests. He retired on 12 November 2025 after 30 years of service. The government commission named him, with Oli and Lekhak, for criminal investigation (Onlinekhabar, 25 March 2026).

evidence.note: End of tenure: Himal Press says he retired on 12 Nov 2025 (Wednesday); Wikipedia's IGP list gives 12 Nov for his end and 13 Nov for Dan Bahadur Karki's start; the cabinet decision naming Karki was on 10 Nov.

properties.profile: 31st Inspector General of Nepal Police, 18 March 2025 to 3 September 2025 (Wikipedia list); replaced by Chandra Kuber Khapung, appointed on 29 August 2025.

Additional IGP at the time of the protests; the NHRC recommended departmental action against him (reported 27 May 2026). Cabinet appointed him Inspector General of Nepal Police on 10 November 2025; Wikipedia lists him as 33rd IGP from 13 November 2025.

evidence.note: Start date: cabinet decision 10 Nov 2025 (Himal Press) versus 13 Nov 2025 (Wikipedia list).

properties.profile: Inspector General of the Armed Police Force during the September 2025 protests. The inquiry commission concluded he failed to give proper direction to his force (Ratopati, 26 March 2026) and recommended action against him (Onlinekhabar). He retired compulsorily on 1 May 2026 after a four-year tenure; Narayan Dutta Poudel took over.

Additional Inspector General promoted to Inspector General of the Armed Police Force, scheduled to take office on 1 May 2026 (Kathmandu Post, 27 April 2026). The name is spelled Narayan Datta Paudel on Wikipedia.
Chief of the Army Staff from 9 September 2021 to 8 September 2024 (Wikipedia); succeeded by Ashok Raj Sigdel. Himal Press says his term ended on 9 September 2024.

evidence.note: End date 8 Sept 2024 (Wikipedia) versus 9 Sept 2024 (Himal Press).

properties.profile: Nepali Congress. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Urban Development from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Wikipedia reports that his Kathmandu residence in Chaksibari was destroyed and that he and his family were helped to safety by the Nepali Army. Not the Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut.
CPN (UML). Minister of Defence from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025; member of the House for Solukhumbu 1.
President of Nepal from 29 October 2015 to 13 March 2023; succeeded by Ram Chandra Paudel. Wikipedia reports that her house in Bhangal, Kathmandu, was burned during the 2025 protests.

Minister of Communication and Information Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 19 January 2026, succeeding Prithvi Subba Gurung; member of the House for Lalitpur 2 since 26 March 2026.

Former Supreme Court justice (1 August 2016-31 October 2023). Minister in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 27 March 2026, holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs and several other portfolios.

Technologist and social entrepreneur. Minister of Education, Science and Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 until he resigned on 20 January 2026 to contest the election. Won Myagdi-1 as an independent in March 2026 and was assigned the science, technology and innovation portfolio on 9 June 2026 (ShareSansar).
Economist and vice chairperson of the Rastriya Swatantra Party since 29 November 2023. Finance Minister in the Balen Shah government since 27 March 2026; member for Tanahun 1.
RSP member for Kathmandu 6. Minister of Foreign Affairs from 27 March 2026; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website names him as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

Retired Supreme Court judge who chaired the commission that investigated the killings and damage of 8-9 September 2025; he handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki (Kathmandu Post, 8 March 2026).
Chairman of Kantipur Publications (Kantipur Media Group), whose headquarters buildings were attacked in September 2025 according to Wikipedia.
Editor-in-chief of The Kathmandu Post (Wikipedia).
Founder, owner and president of the Online Khabar news portal (Wikipedia).

Austrian lawyer; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights since 17 October 2022, succeeding Michelle Bachelet. The Wikipedia article on the 2025 protests lists him among the international officials who commented.
Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission, Nepal, 'since 3rd February 2021' according to the commission's website; a former Supreme Court justice (accessed 2026-10-05).
Chief Election Commissioner of Nepal as listed on Wikipedia (accessed 2026-10-05); the date he took office is not given in the retrieved page.
Justice of the Supreme Court since 1 August 2016; Acting Chief Justice from 1 April to 19 May 2026, after Prakash Man Singh Raut retired.
RSP. Speaker of the House of Representatives since 5 April 2026, succeeding Dev Raj Ghimire. Vice chairperson of the RSP from 2022 to 26 June 2026 and Labour Minister in 2023 and 2024.

Retired Nepal Army lieutenant general who commanded the UN Disengagement Observer Force from 2004. Foreign Minister in the Karki interim government from December 2025 until 27 March 2026, when Shisir Khanal took over.

evidence.note: Start date: 12 Dec 2025 versus 26 Dec 2025 in the Karki cabinet table; Wikipedia's Bala Nanda Sharma page says December 2025 only. Arzu Rana Deuba's page names him as her successor as foreign minister.

properties.profile: Listed on Wikipedia as president of the Nepal Bar Association (accessed 2026-10-05); the date he took office is not given in the retrieved page.
Chief District Officer of Lalitpur. On 9 September 2025 he said the curfew order applied to parts of Lalitpur wards 2, 4, 9, 18 and 25 (Kathmandu Post).
CPN (UML). Chief Minister of Karnali Province from 10 April 2024 to 28 July 2026 (Wikipedia). His residence in Birendranagar was set on fire during the 2025 protests.

Mayor of Dharan from 23 May 2022 to 19 January 2026, elected as an independent; founder of the Shram Sanskriti Party; won Sunsari-1 in 2026. Reported in the 2025 protests article as Harka Raj Rai, Mayor of Dharan.
Last King of Nepal (reigned 2001-2008). In 2025 pro-monarchy crowds gathered around his visits; a rally in Kathmandu on 5 March 2025 backed his possible return (Wikipedia).

Senior Superintendent of Police and Kathmandu police chief on 8 September 2025. The Himalayan Times (10 October 2025) reports testimony that he issued the order to fire; the NHRC later recommended departmental action against a 'Senior SP Bishwa Adhikari'. The accounts are reports of testimony and recommendations, not findings of a court.

evidence.note: Spelling: Bishwo Adhikari (testimony report) versus Bishwa Adhikari (NHRC report).

properties.profile: Home Secretary at the time of the protests, according to the Onlinekhabar report of 25 March 2026, which says the commission recommended action against him under Section 182.

properties.description: Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist-Leninist). Chaired by KP Sharma Oli since 2014. Won 79 seats in the 2022 election, the second largest party. Party led by Baburam Bhattarai from 20 November 2025, formed in the split of the CPN (Maoist Centre) (Wikipedia pages on Bhattarai and the Maoist Centre).
Party whose chairman from 10 January 2026 is Kulman Ghising (Wikipedia).
